title: Find the Bug: Memory Arbitration
statement: A memory arbiter is granting the wrong requester when two requests arrive at once. Your task is to correct the arbitration logic so the highest-priority requester wins and grants remain stable until release. The corrected arbiter must also deassert all grants when no requests are active.
module_signature: module find_bug_memory_arbitration(input clk, input rst, input [2:0] req, output reg [2:0] grant);
behavior: One grant at most may be asserted at a time.
Highest-priority request wins when multiple requests are active.
All state updates occur on the rising edge of clk.
rst is active-high and synchronous unless the problem statement explicitly says otherwise.
Use non-blocking assignments in clocked always blocks.
Outputs must never depend on uninitialized x/z state after reset.
When rst is asserted on a rising edge, registered outputs reset to their documented initial values.
constraints: Avoid asynchronous or combinational grant chasing.
hint: Use a registered grant state and update it each clock cycle.
